    Covariance of S-LDSC Enrichment Estimates from Block-Jackknife Delete Values

    ldsc_jackknife_cov.Rd

    Reconstructs the K x K sampling covariance of the per-topic heritability enrichment estimates from the block-jackknife delete values that S-LDSC writes when run with --print-delete-vals.

    ldsc_jackknife_cov(
  ldsc_res_dir,
  trait,
  nTopics,
  baseline_prefix,
  frq_prefix,
  chrs = 1:22,
  tol_enrichment = 0.01,
  tol_se = 0.05,
  verbose = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    ldsc_res_dir

    Directory holding k*_output/ for each topic, as produced by run_sldsc().

    trait

    Trait name used in the S-LDSC output filenames.

    nTopics

    Number of topics (K).

    baseline_prefix

    Prefix of the baseline annotation files, matching the --ref-ld-chr of the runs being reconstructed, e.g. ".../baselineLD_v2.2/baselineLD.".

    frq_prefix

    Prefix of the PLINK frequency files matching --frqfile-chr, e.g. ".../1000G.EUR.QC.". Used for the MAF 5-50% restriction.

    chrs

    Chromosomes to use. Defaults to 1:22.

    tol_enrichment, tol_se

    Relative tolerances for the acceptance check.

    verbose

    Print per-chromosome progress and the acceptance table.

    Value

    A list with

    Sigma

    the K x K covariance of the enrichment estimates

    check

    per-topic comparison against S-LDSC's reported values

    pass

    TRUE if every topic is within tolerance

    enrichment,se

    the reported point estimates and standard errors

    E_blocks

    n_blocks x K matrix of per-block enrichments

    Details

    This replaces the approximation Cov(e_k, e_m) ~ se_k se_m Cor(A_k, A_m), which substitutes the correlation between annotations for the correlation between their LD scores. That approximation captures only peak overlap: estimates from separate S-LDSC runs are also correlated because they share the GWAS summary statistics, the LD reference panel and the baseline-LD covariates, so two topics with disjoint peak sets still have correlated estimates.

    When it matters

    For the cell score the approximation is usually adequate, because the score's weight vector has a large component along the constant direction where the two agree closely. For cell_type_heterogeneity() it is not: that statistic is constructed to be orthogonal to the constant direction, which is exactly where the approximation error concentrates.

    Method

    Per LD block b, for topic k, $$\hat E_{k,(b)} = \frac{\sum_j \mathrm{overlap}[k,j]\,\tau_{j,(b)}}{\sum_j M_j\,\tau_{j,(b)}} \Big/ \mathrm{Prop.\_SNPs}[k]$$ and Sigma is the ordinary block-jackknife covariance of those vectors. Two details are required for this to reproduce S-LDSC's own output:

    • Overlap correction. S-LDSC reports overlap-corrected per-category heritability (_overlap_output), weighting each category by its overlap with every other annotation. The uncorrected ratio M_k tau_k / sum_j M_j tau_j is a different quantity, and annotations overlap heavily.

    • MAF restriction. When --frqfile-chr is supplied S-LDSC uses M_5_50, so the overlap must be computed over MAF 5-50% variants only.

    With both applied the reconstruction matches the reported Enrichment and Enrichment_std_error to four decimal places; check reports that agreement.

    See also

    get_cs(), cell_type_heterogeneity()
